body:
Save serialization makes many tiny field writes through stdio. This change batches FileManager output in a bounded **16 KiB buffer**, including the checked atomic-save path.

Serialized fields, byte order, SHA1, and autosave cadence are unchanged. Positions include pending bytes; reads, seeks, flushes, and destruction drain in order. Atomic saves retain write/flush/seek/close failure checks before replacement.

### Performance and validation

- Eight-team Playground integration benchmark, holding Cortex optimization fixed: **84.19 s → 71.19 s after buffering**, 15.4% less elapsed time; instructions **1.526T → 1.217T**. Replay, initial save, and final autosave are byte-identical.
- This is an incremental, single-run measurement on integration revision `c71373bb`, not a universal speedup. See `docs/buffered-save-performance.md` for caveats.
- Standalone buffering patch on master, with original Cortex: complete SmallForTwo replay matches the original byte for byte.
- Buffer regression checks bytes/SHA1, boundaries, large writes, backpatching, reads, seeks, flushes, and destruction.
- Existing save-safety tests pass, including atomic/direct byte equivalence, reload checksums, truncated input, and write failures preserving the previous save.
- Buffer tests are added to Linux CI; existing Windows save-safety coverage exercises atomic saving.

This PR contains only output buffering and its tests/documentation. Cortex optimization is independently reviewed in #191. Both target master; neither depends on the other, and unpublished Maxima integration commits are excluded.

comments.body:
@Giszmo Addressed the close/drain bug and integration conflicts through ce29af9a3.

`CheckedFileBackend::close()` now flushes pending bytes and checks stdio errors before closing. `writeAtomically` relies on that checked close instead of pre-flushing, so the existing SavegameSafetyHarness directly exercises pending bytes at close. The base destructor remains best-effort/unchecked, with a brief comment explaining that explicit flush/close provides error reporting.

On macOS, `scons -j6 release=1 server=0 savegame-safety-test buffered-file-test` and both executables pass. Save-safety ran through the shared disposable-profile runner with `--check-preferences`; coverage includes atomic bytes/reload, callback/open/rename failures, injected short write/flush failure, temporary cleanup, corruption controls and the merged pending-construction regression. Buffered-stream checks cover byte/SHA1 equality, boundaries, seeks, reads, flush and destruction. A separate negative-control binary with only the new close flush removed fails in `FileStreamBackend::write` on the null-file assertion, confirming the suite catches this bug.

The first integrated CI exposed a master integration error after #199: ResourceFetchTargetHarness still used getCase. Corrected to getTile here and independently in #215. Ubuntu 22.04, Ubuntu 24.04 and Windows CI all pass: https://github.com/Globulation2/glob2/actions/runs/34300746361 . Please re-review the verified head; no merge performed.

title: Batch save writes while preserving serialization
